── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 30, 32, 35 mi
This week: 32 mi over 5 runs. Planned 36 mi, ran 32 mi.
Pain noted: Thu 2/10 (Outside of right knee tight on the last hill); Sat 1/10 (Knee a little tight before the run, fine during); Sun 4/10 (Outside of right knee, sharp on downhills from mile 7. Walked the last half mile.)
Body: "Right knee aches going down stairs today. Never had this before."
Feeling: "Worried about the knee."
Asks: "Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: The knee is the story of the week, so next week pulls back on quality and distance until a sports physio takes a look. …
Answers: (1) I am not going to name it, because that is a job for a sports physio or sports doctor, not me. … (2) No on Wednesday's tempo. Threshold on a sore knee is exactly how a small niggle becomes a long layoff, and we have 10 weeks to the race, so a quiet week now is cheap insurance.
Safety flag: See a sports physio about the right knee this week
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off to let the knee calm down after Sunday.
Tue: easy, 4 mi, flat route, heart rate under 145, stop if the knee gets sharp. Short…
Wed: other, 30 – 45 min easy bike or pool, no running. Keeps aerobic work in without…
Thu: easy, 4 mi, flat, heart rate under 145. Only if Tuesday felt clean, otherwise…
Fri: rest. Usual rest day, let the week settle.
Sat: easy, 3 mi, flat, conversational. Short shakeout before Sunday.
Sun: long, 8 mi easy, flat route, heart rate under 150, walk breaks are fine. Shorter…
